text: 4 августа группировка войск "Север" продолжила создание полосы безопасности в Харьковской и Сумской областях #Группировка_войск_Север В Черниговской области усилились рейды миграционных служб Украины, которые на своих официальных ресурсах прямо сообщают, что единственная возможность для трудовых мигрантов избежать задержания - пройти службу в ВСУ. На Сумском направлении Штурмовики ГВ "Север" продолжают продвигаться вглубь Сумской области. Наши войска нанесли удары по скоплениям живой силы и техники противника в районах города Сумы, сёл Садки и Новые Вирки , Глухова и Краснополья. В Шосткинском районе стрелковые бои идут в Уланово и на подступах к Вольной Слободе. В районе Рыжевки зафиксированы боестолкновения между националистами 125 отмбр ВСУ и 103 обр ТерО . Предварительной причиной конфликта стало бегство солдат львовской бригады теробороны с занимаемых позиций. В Сумском районе наши штурмовики продвинулись на шестнадцати участках до 700 метров. Не прекращаются стрелковые бои в Рыжевке, Писаревке , Марьино, посёлке Хотень , окрестностях населенных пунктов , а также в лесных массивах южнее Иволжанского. В Краснопольском районе враг силами трёх боевых групп из состава 119 обр ТерО

text: Группировка войск "Север" освободила село Рыжевка Сумской области! Штурмовые подразделения 1427 мсп 11 АК ГВ "Север" в ходе ожесточенных боев выбили националистов 125 отмбр и 103 обр ТерО из села Рыжевка Сумского района и освободили населенный пункт. Накануне часть солдат львовской территориальной обороны бежала с занимаемых позиций в районе Рыжевки, что привело к разгрому оставшихся националистов из состава 125 отмбр, побратимы которых решили "воспитать" солдат 103 обр ТерО заградительным огнём. Характерно, что территориальная оборона ответила из стрелкового оружия по союзному подразделению... Также стоит отметить, что в настоящее время 103 обр ТерО активно комплектуется из депортированных украинцев, многие из которых проживали в странах ЕС задолго до начала СВО. Освобождение Рыжевки является важным этапом в создании полосы безопасности в Сумской области и минимизирует риски проникновения вражеских ДРГ в многострадальный посёлок Тёткино Глушковского района Курской области. @warriorofnorth

title: Mexican influencer shot dead while streaming live on social media
text: César Gastélum had nearly 600,000 followers on TikTok and was known for making comedy videos. Photograph: Instagram/cesarselectivo/Reuters View image in fullscreen César Gastélum had nearly 600,000 followers on TikTok and was known for making comedy videos. Photograph: Instagram/cesarselectivo/Reuters Mexico Mexican influencer shot dead while streaming live on social media César Gastélum was filming outside a fast-food outlet in Sinaloa state when he was killed by a motorbike driver Oscar Lopez in Mexico City Wed 5 Aug 2026 13.31 EDT Last modified on Wed 5 Aug 2026 13.48 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A popular Mexican influencer has been shot dead while doing a live stream on social media outside a restaurant in Sinaloa state, where lethal cartel violence has become widespread. César Gastélum, who had nearly 600,000 followers on TikTok and was known for making comedy videos, was filming with two friends outside a fast-food restaurant in the city of Culiacán. The three were dressed in the bright orange jackets and backpacks of food delivery drivers. A motorcycle with a driver and pillion rider suddenly pulled up beside them and the driver pulled out a gun and shot Gastélum
author: Oscar Lopez in Mexico City

title: New Zealand capital delights in rare snowfall as southern city residents ski down world’s steepest street
text: Snow in the New Zealand city of Dunedin. Photograph: Mark Stevenson View image in fullscreen Snow in the New Zealand city of Dunedin. Photograph: Mark Stevenson New Zealand New Zealand capital delights in rare snowfall as southern city residents ski down world’s steepest street Snow falls in Wellington for the first time in 15 years while snow blanketed Dunedin and Christchurch on the country’s south island Eva Corlett in Wellington Tue 4 Aug 2026 23.27 EDT Last modified on Thu 6 Aug 2026 03.44 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Temperatures have plummeted across New Zealand as an Antarctic cold snap hovers over the country, delighting the capital, Wellington, which experienced snow for the first time in 15 years, while giving a southern city’s residents a chance to ski through the streets. The front moved in on Tuesday, with much of the country waking to freezing conditions, frosts, snowfall, hail and bitingly cold wind. Conditions persisted on Wednesday morning, with three South Island locations reaching -9C. Some highways were closed, while parts of the North Island’s east coast woke to thick hail storms. title: Can ‘Russia’s Amazon’ Survive Ukraine’s Drone Campaign?
text: Can ‘Russia’s Amazon’ Survive Ukraine’s Drone Campaign? By Moscow Times Reporter Aug. 5, 2026 Electronic screens advertise the Wildberries online retailer in Moscow. Reuters / Anastasia Barashkova A wave of Ukrainian drone attacks has knocked out more than a quarter of Wildberries’ warehouse capacity, threatening to disrupt the logistics network behind Russia’s largest online retailer and inflict billions of dollars in losses on the company and its sellers. Analysts say the attacks are unlikely to pose a serious threat to Russia’s wider economy. title: Japan Protests Russian Military Drills Near Disputed Kuril Islands
text: Japan Protests Russian Military Drills Near Disputed Kuril Islands Aug. 5, 2026 Russian Defense Ministry Japan has lodged a diplomatic protest over Russian military exercises taking place around the disputed southern Kuril Islands, Japanese media reported Wednesday. Russia’s Defense Ministry announced the military drills on Tuesday, saying they will involve 60 warships, 30 aircraft and more than 13,000 servicemen in the Sea of Japan, the Sea of Okhotsk and the northwestern Pacific Ocean. According to the Sankei Shimbun newspaper, Russia notified Japanese officials that it will hold multi-day live-fire exercises around two of the four Kuril Islands, which Tokyo claims as its Northern Territories. Russia also designated maritime exclusion zones around the remaining two islands for drills running through Aug. 29, along with missile test warnings through Aug. 6, the newspaper added. title: Putin Announces Reshuffling of Top Military Leadership
text: Putin Announces Reshuffling of Top Military Leadership Aug. 5, 2026 Putin meets with top Defense Ministry officials at the Kremlin. kremlin.ru President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday announced a major reshuffle across the top ranks of Russia’s military, appointing new operational commanders in Ukraine, a unified logistics chief and a head for the newly established drone warfare branch. “We’re continuing to refine the Defense Ministry’s organizational structure to keep pace with the needs and lessons learned from the special military operation,” Putin said in a televised Kremlin meeting, using the official term for Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. As part of the reshuffle, the president appointed Colonel General Denis Lyamin to head Russia’s newly established Unmanned Systems Forces. Putin also reorganized frontline leadership in eastern and southern Ukraine, naming Colonel General Andrei Ivanayev commander of the “Center” group of forces and Lieutenant General Pyotr Bolgarev commander of the “East” group. Putin also reorganized leadership within Russia’s operational fronts in eastern and southern Ukraine, naming Colonel General Andrei Ivanayev commander of the “Center” group

title: FSB Arrests Kaluga Man Accused of Plotting Attack on Military Enlistment Office
text: FSB Arrests Kaluga Man Accused of Plotting Attack on Military Enlistment Office Aug. 5, 2026 FSB officers arrest a man in the Kaluga region accused of plotting an attack on a military enlistment office. FSB Russia’s FSB security service said Wednesday that it arrested a man who was suspected of plotting an arson attack against a military enlistment office in the central Kaluga region on orders from Ukraine. In an FSB video aired by state media, the 22-year-old man, whose face was blurred, said an officer from Ukraine’s military intelligence service offered him money to carry out a series of criminal acts. “First, I was tasked with putting up graffiti discrediting the Russian government, and then burning down a military enlistment office,” the man said in the video, adding that he had been in contact with his handler for around a year before his arrest. FSB officers seized several canisters of flammable liquid along with electronic devices containing chat logs between the suspect and his handler, the law enforcement agency said. title: After deadly Kyiv strike, Ukraine warns interceptor shortage is costing lives
text: After deadly Kyiv strike, Ukraine warns interceptor shortage is costing lives Figure caption, Watch: 'Scariest night' as Ukraine fails to intercept Russian attack By Dan Johnson Ukraine correspondent in Kyiv Published 5 August 2026 At the Kvitneva railway station near Kyiv, workers lift white body bags from the pockmarked platform and carry them to waiting ambulances. Shoes, glasses and some pieces of clothing mark the spot where eight people were killed during Russia's latest massive aerial attack on Ukraine. Overnight, Moscow fired 115 drones and 24 ballistic missiles. Most of the drones were shot down, but Kyiv's depleted air defences did not intercept any of the missiles. Twenty-one people were killed and dozens more were injured. The latest Russian barrage destroyed storage and logistics facilities - from online retailer warehouses to a postal sorting centre. In Kvitneva, it is not clear if the target was the railway itself or the warehouse beside it, which was also hit and was still smouldering hours later. title: Fire Breaks Out at Main Roscosmos Research Center Near Moscow
text: Fire Breaks Out at Main Roscosmos Research Center Near Moscow Aug. 5, 2026 Smoke and fire at TsNIIMash. Telegram A fire briefly broke out Wednesday at the leading research center for Russia’s space agency, Roscosmos, triggering an evacuation of staff. Roscosmos said a fire alarm sounded around 1 p.m. local time after smoke was detected in the basement of a building at the Central Research Institute of Machine Building (TsNIIMash) in the town of Korolyov, located outside of Moscow. Staff were evacuated as firefighters responded to put out the blaze. No injuries were reported, the space agency said. Russian media released videos showing dark smoke rising above the complex, which houses mission control for the Russian segment of the International Space Station. Roscosmos said there was no threat to workers or nearby residents, noting that ISS operations “remain fully under the control of specialists.” An internal commission will determine the cause of the fire once the site is fully cleared, the agency added. text: Yekaterinburg Drone Maker CEO Wounded in Car Explosion Aug. 5, 2026 Vladimir Tkachuk. @urfo_info / Telegram The head of a Russian drone manufacturer was seriously wounded in a car explosion, Russian media reported Wednesday, in what appears to be the second attempted assassination of a defense executive in Russia over the past week. Vladimir Tkachuk is the founder and CEO of the Yekaterinburg-based firm Uraldronzavod. The company is under U.S. and EU sanctions for producing the Upyr drone, which is widely used in Russia’s war against Ukraine. Tkachuk also runs a popular pro-war Telegram channel, Povornutye Na Voyne, which confirmed that an “assassination attempt” had taken place following news reports of the car explosion. “He’s currently in intensive care and in stable condition,” the channel added. However, sources told the state-run news agency TASS that Tkachuk was in critical condition and that doctors were “fighting for his life.” Eyewitnesses told local media they heard a loud explosion and saw flames engulf Tkachuk’s Mercedes in Bolshoy Istok, a village just outside Yekaterinburg. title: Russia Says Its HIV Rates Are Falling. Experts Aren’t So Sure.
text: Russia Says Its HIV Rates Are Falling. Experts Aren’t So Sure. By Moscow Times Reporter Aug. 5, 2026 HIV Testing at a Clinic in Moscow. Moskva News Agency Four years ago, while hospitalized with Covid-19, St. Petersburg singer Ksenia Aleksandrova was unexpectedly diagnosed with HIV. Known by her stage name Neksusha, the 23-year-old Aleksandrova has built a devoted online following, with around 90,000 subscribers on YouTube and more than 213,000 monthly listeners on Spotify. Despite the persistent stigma that surrounds HIV, she decided to publicly disclose her diagnosis in an effort to raise awareness about the illness. “I’m not a drug user, I’m not a sex worker. It just happened, I’ve been in a monogamous relationship for a year and my partner is HIV-negative,” she told journalists at the time. “I realized I was tired of staying silent. I have a platform and I want to use my story to help other people,” she said . Since then, Neksusha has openly discussed HIV, using her social media to educate her audience in Russia. title: Putin Announces Reshuffling of Top Military Leadership
text: Putin Announces Reshuffling of Top Military Leadership Aug. 5, 2026 Putin meets with top Defense Ministry officials at the Kremlin. kremlin.ru President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday announced a major reshuffle across the top ranks of Russia’s military, appointing new operational commanders in Ukraine, a unified logistics chief and a head for the newly established drone warfare branch. “We’re continuing to refine the Defense Ministry’s organizational structure to keep pace with the needs and lessons learned from the special military operation,” Putin said in a televised Kremlin meeting, using the official term for Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. As part of the reshuffle, the president appointed Colonel General Denis Lyamin to head Russia’s newly established Unmanned Systems Forces. Putin also reorganized frontline leadership in eastern and southern Ukraine, naming Colonel General Andrei Ivanayev commander of the “Center” group of forces and Lieutenant General Pyotr Bolgarev commander of the “East” group. Putin also reorganized leadership within Russia’s operational fronts in eastern and southern Ukraine, naming Colonel General Andrei Ivanayev commander of the “Center” group

text: FSB Arrests Kaluga Man Accused of Plotting Attack on Military Enlistment Office Aug. 5, 2026 FSB officers arrest a man in the Kaluga region accused of plotting an attack on a military enlistment office. FSB Russia’s FSB security service said Wednesday that it arrested a man who was suspected of plotting an arson attack against a military enlistment office in the central Kaluga region on orders from Ukraine. In an FSB video aired by state media, the 22-year-old man, whose face was blurred, said an officer from Ukraine’s military intelligence service offered him money to carry out a series of criminal acts. “First, I was tasked with putting up graffiti discrediting the Russian government, and then burning down a military enlistment office,” the man said in the video, adding that he had been in contact with his handler for around a year before his arrest. title: Secret funeral reportedly held in Moscow for unnamed major general. He may have died in an assassination attempt on Russian Aerospace Forces chief Alexander Chayko.
text: An unnamed major general was buried at Moscow’s Troekurovskoye Cemetery, the anonymous Russian Telegram channel VChK-OGPU reported. The channel’s authors said he may have been a friend of Aerospace Forces Commander-in-Chief Alexander Chayko and died in the explosion at the Balzi Rossi restaurant. The funeral was held in secrecy, the channel wrote. Federal Protective Service and Russian National Guard officers were stationed at the cemetery from early morning, inspecting every vehicle that entered and requiring visitors to pass through security scanners. Eyewitnesses said the major general being buried was “fairly young” and had previously served in the Ground Forces. A Russian Ground Forces flag stood next to the grave. An honor guard carrying a flag of Russia’s Aerospace Forces accompanied the procession. The Telegram channel did not name the major general, and its authors said they could not confirm he was actually at the Balzi Rossi restaurant when the explosion occurred. A homemade explosive device detonated at the Balzi Rossi restaurant in Moscow on August 1, killing five people — three at the scene and two more later in the hospital — and injuring another 19. title: Putin has reshuffled Russia’s military command. Here’s what you need to know.
text: Denis Lyamin (left) and Valery Solodchuk. August 5, 2026. On August 5, at a meeting with Defense Ministry leadership, Vladimir Putin announced several major changes in military command all at once. “We continue to improve the structure of the Defense Ministry in light of the needs and experience of the special military operation,” the president said, explaining the changes. Here’s who received new appointments. Unmanned Systems Forces New commander : Colonel General Denis Lyamin, who most recently served as chief of staff of the Tsentr grouping. Lyamin took command of the 58th Army in 2023 after his predecessor, Ivan Popov, was dismissed for publicly criticizing the Defense Ministry’s leadership. Popov later received a five-year sentence in a penal colony on fraud charges. The Unmanned Systems Forces is a new branch of the military that the Defense Ministry announced had been fully formed as of December 2025. text: Former European and Russian Officials Held Secret Talks in Austria – Bloomberg Aug. 5, 2026 Simon Walker / No 10 Downing Street Former diplomats and national security officials from Europe and Russia met secretly in Vienna last month to explore potential terms for holding peace talks with Ukraine, Bloomberg reported Wednesday, citing sources familiar with the matter. The Western figures included former British national security adviser Tim Barrow, former German State Secretary Markus Ederer and veteran French diplomat Pierre Vimont. The former Russian official’s identity was not disclosed. The Kremlin has not commented on the reported meeting. title: After deadly Kyiv strike, Ukraine warns interceptor shortage is costing lives
text: After deadly Kyiv strike, Ukraine warns interceptor shortage is costing lives Figure caption, Watch: 'Scariest night' as Ukraine fails to intercept Russian attack By Dan Johnson Ukraine correspondent in Kyiv Published 5 August 2026 At the Kvitneva railway station near Kyiv, workers lift white body bags from the pockmarked platform and carry them to waiting ambulances. Shoes, glasses and some pieces of clothing mark the spot where eight people were killed during Russia's latest massive aerial attack on Ukraine. Overnight, Moscow fired 115 drones and 24 ballistic missiles. Most of the drones were shot down, but Kyiv's depleted air defences did not intercept any of the missiles. Twenty-one people were killed and dozens more were injured. The latest Russian barrage destroyed storage and logistics facilities - from online retailer warehouses to a postal sorting centre. In Kvitneva, it is not clear if the target was the railway itself or the warehouse beside it, which was also hit and was still smouldering hours later. title: Can ‘Russia’s Amazon’ Survive Ukraine’s Drone Campaign?
text: Can ‘Russia’s Amazon’ Survive Ukraine’s Drone Campaign? By Moscow Times Reporter Aug. 5, 2026 Electronic screens advertise the Wildberries online retailer in Moscow. Reuters / Anastasia Barashkova A wave of Ukrainian drone attacks has knocked out more than a quarter of Wildberries’ warehouse capacity, threatening to disrupt the logistics network behind Russia’s largest online retailer and inflict billions of dollars in losses on the company and its sellers. Analysts say the attacks are unlikely to pose a serious threat to Russia’s wider economy. But a prolonged campaign could drive up Wildberries’ costs, delay deliveries and weaken its grip on a fiercely competitive market that has expanded rapidly since Western brands left Russia following the invasion of Ukraine. The campaign, which began on July 18, has repeatedly targeted facilities where merchants’ goods are stored before being shipped to customers. Kyiv has accused Wildberries of supplying the Russian military with drone components and other equipment. title: Fire Breaks Out at Main Roscosmos Research Center Near Moscow
text: Fire Breaks Out at Main Roscosmos Research Center Near Moscow Aug. 5, 2026 Smoke and fire at TsNIIMash. Telegram A fire briefly broke out Wednesday at the leading research center for Russia’s space agency, Roscosmos, triggering an evacuation of staff. Roscosmos said a fire alarm sounded around 1 p.m. local time after smoke was detected in the basement of a building at the Central Research Institute of Machine Building (TsNIIMash) in the town of Korolyov, located outside of Moscow. Staff were evacuated as firefighters responded to put out the blaze. No injuries were reported, the space agency said. Russian media released videos showing dark smoke rising above the complex, which houses mission control for the Russian segment of the International Space Station. Roscosmos said there was no threat to workers or nearby residents, noting that ISS operations “remain fully under the control of specialists.” An internal commission will determine the cause of the fire once the site is fully cleared, the agency added.
